app.d21cbb1d4cc8a934: A complete guide to building, tracking, and displaying your live checklist.
app.5b0774deb3b682fe:
1. Create a build and make it active

Open Build Progression from the Live Stats tab. Your library can hold multiple builds: create, configure, duplicate, delete, import, or export them as JSON files.

Only one build is tracked at a time. Select Set Active on its library card; editing another build does not activate it.
app.10183f78276bccba:
2. Add and arrange requirements

Choose a target from the catalog, enter its required value, configure an optional deadline, and add it to the checklist. Existing rows can be edited, reordered, or removed before you save the build.

• Items track copies in the inventory.
• Stats track live player attributes; the editor handles percentage and multiplier display formats for you.
• Progress tracks whole-number run goals such as Kills and Player Level.
app.4467785124aeea65:
3. Min, Max, Ideal, and Cap targets

The required value is the Min. An item may also have a Max, and a stat may have an Ideal. Once Min is reached, the displayed target switches to Max or Ideal and stays active until that second target is reached. The live checklist shows only the new number, without a Max or Ideal label.

Supported radius items can use Cap instead of a fixed Max. Cap starts with the first copy and calculates the remaining copies from the captured Size stat; it updates as the run changes. An em dash means the cap cannot be resolved yet.

Progress requirements use one target only.
app.603ae9e3a8cf3726:
4. Deadlines apply to Min

Choose No deadline, Before tier, or Tier overtime. Before tier must be completed before that tier starts. Tier overtime sets a deadline after the selected tier’s main timer ends.

The deadline judges when Min was first reached. Reaching Max, Ideal, or Cap later does not make an on-time Min late. If Min was late, that late result remains visible while the second target is active and after the full requirement is completed.

A deadline turns yellow in its final two minutes and red when overdue.
app.ac088aecf6b1ddfc:
5. Read the live checklist

Rows are grouped as Items, Stats, then Progress. Item names use rarity colours, Stats are blue, and Progress is teal. Symbols and deadline colours show whether a row is active, completed on time, or completed late.

Within each group, active Min targets come first, followed by active Max, Ideal, or Cap targets and then rows without deadlines. Completed-on-time rows follow, then rows completed late, with overdue unfinished requirements at the end. Active Min targets with the nearest deadlines rise within their group.
app.9e91ad2bd492d4d5:
6. Control what remains visible

Turn Show completed off to remove every fully completed row, including requirements completed late. A row that has reached Min but is still working toward Max, Ideal, or Cap remains visible because it is still active.

The row limit caps how many unfinished requirements are shown. When nothing remains, the widget collapses to the build-complete state.
app.d4578d6f9bdfaec6:
7. One active build, several live surfaces

The same active build and runtime progress are shared by the Live Stats tab, OBS widget, in-game overlay, and Twitch !build command. Changing the active build updates every surface.

Display controls are independent: OBS and the in-game overlay keep their own enabled state, scale, row limit, and Show completed preference where available.

app.e71825bf43296470: A step-by-step guide to what the scanner counts and why a map passes or fails.
app.dde758cb1465fceb:
1. What is Score?

Score is one number that represents how valuable the generated map is according to your settings. The scanner counts Moais, Shady Guys, Boss Curses, Magnet Shrines, and Challenges. Each count is converted into points, then all points are added together.
app.1f3ebb492b8b8581:
2. What does each Shrine Points value mean?

The number beside a shrine is the amount added for each one found on the map.

• Positive value: you want this shrine. For example, Moais = 3 means every Moai adds 3 points. Four Moais add 12.
• Zero: this shrine does not change Score. It is still shown in map statistics, but whether the map has zero or ten makes no difference to Scores mode.
• Negative value: you do not want this shrine. For example, Challenges = -3 means every Challenge removes 3 points. Two Challenges remove 6.

All five Shrine Points fields accept positive, zero, and negative values.
app.688e656156838ed2:
3. How is the base score calculated?

For every shrine type, the scanner multiplies the map count by its configured Shrine Points value:

Base Score =
(Moais × Moai points)
+ (Shady Guys × Shady points)
+ (Boss Curses × Boss points)
+ (Magnet Shrines × Magnet points)
+ (Challenges × Challenge points)

Negative results are simply subtracted. A penalty is soft: it lowers the number, but it never rejects a map by itself. Enough positive shrines can compensate for it.
app.2679b875ce38c7d0:
4. How are Magnet Shrines counted?

Every Magnet Shrine uses the configured Magnet points value. Positive values reward every Magnet, zero ignores them, and negative values penalize every Magnet. There is no two-Magnet cap.
app.de7cb2f5ec4ba2ae:
5. When is the Microwave multiplier applied?

The scanner first finishes the entire Base Score calculation, including every reward and penalty. Only then is the whole result multiplied by the Microwave value.

Final Score = Base Score × Microwave Multiplier

This means the multiplier affects penalties too. A Base Score of 24 with a 1.25 multiplier becomes a Final Score of 30.
app.10b3dfc209e3a3bb:
6. Full example

Settings: Moai = 3, Shady = 2, Boss = 1, Magnet = -1, Challenges = -3, and the two-Microwave multiplier = 1.25.

Map: 4 Moais, 5 Shady Guys, 3 Boss Curses, 1 Magnet, 0 Challenges, and 2 Microwaves.

Moais: 4 × 3 = 12
Shady Guys: 5 × 2 = 10
Boss Curses: 3 × 1 = 3
Magnet: 1 × -1 = -1
Challenges: 0 × -3 = 0

Base Score: 12 + 10 + 3 - 1 + 0 = 24
Final Score: 24 × 1.25 = 30
app.64f26e43f193d32d:
7. What are thresholds and active tiers?

A threshold is the minimum Final Score needed for a tier. If Light is 14, a map with 13.9 fails Light and a map with 14 passes it.

Only enabled tiers can stop the scanner. The scanner stops as soon as the map reaches any enabled tier. Enabling Light means a Light-or-better map may stop the scan; enabling every tier does not make the scanner wait specifically for Perfect+.
app.b5e00cf6093a2557:
8. Extra Perfect and Perfect+ requirements

Reaching the number alone is not always enough:

• Perfect+: the score must reach its threshold and the map must have at least 2 Microwaves.
• Perfect: the score must reach its threshold and the map must have either 2 Microwaves, or 1 Microwave together with at least 8 total Shady Guys + Moais and at least 2 Boss Curses.
• Good and Light: only their score threshold is checked.
app.5c262324685389d1:
9. Automatic vs Manual Thresholds

Automatic Thresholds scale the tier targets when you change positive Shrine Points and use the stronger positive Microwave multiplier as the reference. Negative values are excluded from this scaling, so making a penalty stronger never makes the target easier.

If every Shrine Points value is zero or negative, automatic targets cannot be calculated usefully. The same is true if both Microwave multipliers are zero. Add a positive value or enable Manual Thresholds and enter the tier targets yourself.

app.106c6ebd7c0b22cb:

Quick Reset

app.b2c4d4e395198b92:
2. Set the reset key hold

In BonkScanner Settings → Restart, Reset key hold is how long the reset key stays pressed. A shorter hold can make resets faster; map loading also affects the time between runs.

Use recommended values applies game 0.01 s + extra 0.05 s = hold 0.06 s. On a new installation, this setup is applied when the game is closed. If it could not be applied, close the game and use this button in Settings. The hold must cover the game's reset threshold plus Extra hold time (Safety Margin). For example: game 0.20 s + extra 0.05 s = hold 0.25 s.

With your {p0:.2f}-second safety margin, the lowest selectable hold is {p1:.2f} s (game minimum {p2:.2f} s).

Settings shows the current game-file value and what Save will change. Close Megabonk only if its config needs changing. A game-file change takes effect on the next game launch. Changed config files are verified.
